accepted.s: In the estimation of the household or unincorporated sector, which of the following methods is used?
o: It is estimated exclusively from MCA-21 company filings
It is benchmarked on ASUSE and extrapolated using indicators
It is estimated only through PLFS employment data
It is benchmarked on the ASI and extrapolated using CPI
accepted.x: The household or unincorporated sector is benchmarked on ASUSE and subsequently extrapolated with suitable indicators. MCA-21 covers companies, while PLFS provides employment data.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct survey-method relationship and reject exclusive wording.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly indicates the principal coverage of MCA-21 in the estimation of national accounts?
accepted.x: MCA-21 provides data relating to companies. Household consumption, registered factories and time use are covered through other sources.
accepted.tq: Match the data source with the sector or unit it covers.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional sectors used in national accounts:
1. General government is one of the four institutional sectors.
2. Public corporations are one of the four institutional sectors.
3. Household and private corporation sectors are also included.
4. Data relating to government and public corporations are generally the most robust.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The four institutional sectors are general government, public corporations, private corporations and households. Among them, government and public-corporation data are regarded as the most robust.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each statement is directly supported.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Which survey is specifically associated with employment, unemployment, labour force participation rate and worker population ratio?
accepted.x: PLFS measures employment, unemployment, LFPR and WPR through monthly, quarterly and annual estimates.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the survey from its statistical indicators.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Survey)
a. HCES
b. ASI
c. ASUSE
 d. TUS
List-II (Coverage)
i. Time use and paid or unpaid work
ii. Household consumption and CPI weights
iii. Registered factory sector
iv. Unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: HCES covers household consumption, ASI covers registered factories, ASUSE covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises and TUS covers time use.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure survey-coverage pairs and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: The Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) primarily covers:
accepted.x: ASUSE is designed to cover unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises, which form an important part of the informal sector.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named enterprise surveys.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Which one of the following surveys is associated with paid and unpaid work?
accepted.x: The Time Use Survey measures the time spent on paid and unpaid work.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive subject of the survey to identify the answer.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent statistical survey initiatives is correct?
o: The Household Income Survey replaces PLFS and measures only factory employment.
The Household Income Survey and Common Property Resources survey are new initiatives, while the SAS of rural agricultural households is scheduled for 2026–27.
The SAS of rural agricultural households was discontinued after 2025.
The Common Property Resources survey is confined to incorporated service enterprises.
accepted.x: The Household Income Survey and Common Property Resources survey are identified as new initiatives. The SAS of rural agricultural households is scheduled for 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Reject statements that assign a neighbouring survey an incorrect purpose or status.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s:
With reference to the revised PLFS and ASUSE arrangements, consider the following statements:
1. PLFS 2025 provides monthly all-India estimates.
2. PLFS 2025 provides quarterly rural estimates.
3. ASUSE 2025 permits quarterly estimates.
4. District-level PLFS and ASUSE estimates are expected by 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the recent expansion of PLFS and ASUSE estimation arrangements.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of linked reforms through an all-statements option.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Reports under the revised statistical arrangements are generally expected within which time period, while monthly results are expected within which shorter period?
accepted.x: The stated reporting period is 45–90 days, while monthly results are expected within 15 days.
accepted.tq: Compare the paired time limits rather than treating the figures independently.
accepted.sec: Informal sector estimation - methods and data

accepted.s: Which institution publishes national income and GDP estimates in India?
o: State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
accepted.x: National income and GDP estimates are published by the NSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; the table also identifies the earlier CSO association.
accepted.tq: Identify the publishing body from the statistic concerned.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is published by the NSO and is ordinarily released:
o: On the 28th of every month through 14 source agencies
On the last working day of every quarter through State DES
On the 15th of every month through one source agency
On the 7th of every month through the Labour Bureau
accepted.x: IIP is published by NSO, released monthly on the 28th, and draws on 14 source agencies. The new series has a lag of 28 days.
accepted.tq: Combine the publishing body, release date and source-agency count.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: The new IIP series is associated with a lag of:
accepted.x: The new IIP series is released with a lag of 28 days.
accepted.tq: Test the precise numerical feature attached to a statistical series.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: The Consumer Price Index for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the NSO. The new series mentioned for this index was released on:
accepted.x: The new CPI Rural/Urban/Combined series was released on 12 February 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely dated releases by linking the date to the correct index.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: The new CPI series released in February 2026 follows COICOP 2018 and expands the number of groups from:
accepted.x: The new CPI series follows COICOP 2018 and expands the groups from 6 to 12.
accepted.tq: Test the exact before-and-after range in a statistical classification.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the agency associated with the Wholesale Price Index?
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Labour Bureau, Chandigarh, Ministry of Labour
accepted.x: The WPI is associated with the Office of the Economic Adviser under DPIIT in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-and-body swap trap used in economic statistics questions.
accepted.sec: Statistic → publishing body

accepted.s: Which organisation prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail?
o: State DES through GSDP accounts only
DPIIT through the Office of the Economic Adviser
accepted.x: MoSPI/NSO prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail.
accepted.tq: Identify the agency responsible for the complete group of related estimates.
accepted.sec: Savings and capital formation estimates - agency and sector shares

accepted.s: The institutional sectors specifically identified for savings and capital-formation estimates are:
o: General government, labour and foreign sectors
Household, private corporate and public sectors
accepted.x: The sectors identified for these estimates are household, private corporate and public sectors.
accepted.tq: Separate institutional-sector classification from production-sector classification.
accepted.sec: Savings and capital formation estimates - agency and sector shares

accepted.s: The private corporate sector's share of Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF) was reported as:
accepted.x: The private corporate share of GFCF was 33 per cent, described as a decadal low.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed trend trap between a share and its historical position.
accepted.sec: Savings and capital formation estimates - agency and sector shares

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the recent national accounts developments is correct?
o: The GDP release date moved to 12 February, coinciding with the new CPI series.
The 2022–23 series was introduced only after the 2026–27 agricultural household survey.
The 2022–23 series was released on 7 June 2026, while GDP releases moved to 27 February.
The 2022–23 series was associated with a 27 February 2026 release, and the GDP release date moved to 7 June 2026.
accepted.x: The 2022–23 series was associated with 27 February 2026, and the GDP release date moved to 7 June 2026.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among several nearby dates associated with different releases.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following issues has been identified in current debates concerning national accounts?
o: The discontinuation of ASUSE and PLFS
The replacement of CPI-IW by GSDP
The abolition of all institutional-sector estimates
Coverage of the informal sector and MCA-based manufacturing GVA
accepted.x: Current criticism and debate concern the coverage of the informal sector and the use of MCA-based manufacturing GVA. IMF data concerns have also been raised.
accepted.tq: Select the substantive criticism rather than an absolute institutional change.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement correctly reflects the relation between NSO and international statistical standards?
o: NSO follows IMF-SDDS norms and is the nodal agency for the ICP in India.
NSO follows only WPI norms and has no role in the ICP.
NSO is the nodal agency for CPI-IW but not for the ICP.
NSO follows Labour Bureau standards for all national accounts estimates.
accepted.x: The NSO follows IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard norms and acts as India's nodal agency for the International Comparison Programme.
accepted.tq: Pair the institution with both its standard-setting framework and international role.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: India was identified as the third-largest economy by purchasing power parity in the context of which programme?
o: Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises, 2025
accepted.x: India was identified as the third-largest economy by PPP in the International Comparison Programme 2021.
accepted.tq: Link the ranking to the programme and reference year rather than to a domestic survey.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES-AP) moved towards which base-year arrangement under the MoSPI GSVA guideline?
accepted.x: DES-AP moved towards the 2022–23 base under the MoSPI GSVA guideline.
accepted.tq: Test the state-level application of the national base-year revision.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding statistical developments in 2026:
1. The new GDP series based on 2022–23 was released in February 2026.
2. The new IIP series based on 2022–23 was released in February 2026.
3. The new CPI series based on 2024 was released in February 2026.
4. The first CPI print on the new base was 2.75 per cent in January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the release timing, base years and the first CPI print of 2.75 per cent in January 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the common release month while checking each series-specific base and figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh-specific statistical arrangements?
o: AP DES compiles only national GDP and has no role in CPI-IW.
AP DES compiles WPI exclusively for the Union Government.
AP DES compiles GSDP and a State CPI-IW series; Vijayawada was dropped as a CPI-IW centre in the 2016 series.
Vijayawada became the sole CPI-IW centre in the 2016 series.
accepted.x: AP DES compiles GSDP and a State CPI-IW series. Vijayawada was dropped as a CPI-IW centre in the 2016 series.
accepted.tq: Combine two state-specific facts and reject incorrect institutional assignments.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
